title: Eight HBM3e stacks (1228 B/cycle each) against the Argon2id memory architecture
status: measured in RTL simulation; analytic figures separated below

sim.clock: 1 GHz equivalent (1 ns timescale, B/cycle == GB/s)
commands: ssh airobots@192.168.1.15 'cd ~/anubis-solver/chip && make -B B=build/<tag> hbm3e-mpipe MP_NENG=N MP_CYC=C MP_NSTACK=S MP_TARGET=10000'

spec.hbm3e_per_stack: 9.6 Gb/s/pin x 1024 bit / 8 = 1228.8 GB/s = 1228.8 B/cycle at 1 GHz
spec.pyhsical_note: 8 x 16 GiB = 128 GiB of stacks, but Argon2id m=19456 KiB needs only 19 MiB resident: the stacks are bought for bandwidth, not capacity

measured_capacity.result: PASS: all 8 links run at 1228 B/cycle independently; aggregate 9824 B/cycle

measured_router.description: tb_hbm3e_capacity, one hbm3e_mem #(NSTACK=8), single request port, blk++ on every accept, 1024 cycles

independence_test.result: PASS: req_ready is the selected stack's ready only, an unrelated busy stack cannot stall a request

measured_router.result: PASS: merged responses intact, 12.50% per stack
measured_router.port_limit_note: 4096 B/cycle is the single request port (one 4096 B request per cycle), not the memory: only 42% of the 9824 B/cycle of stacks are used

measured_sweep.dut: argon2_mpipe (KCTX=2, IDW=clog2(NENG*KCTX)) -> hbm3e_mem -> 8 x hbm3_model #(BW=1228, LAT=350, EFF=100)

long_run_236_c260_60000cyc.note: the 13.08/11.92 split at 10k cycles relaxes to 12.60/12.40 over 60k cycles: the router is even, the mpipe traffic is not (all context start offsets are even multiples of BPH/NCTX = 82)

findings: The eight links are real: measured 1228.0 B/cycle each and 9824.0 B/cycle aggregate, 0.0% error against the analytic 9824 (one request port per stack).

The single request port is the wall, not the DRAM: 8 stacks reach only 3578 B/cycle (36% of 9.82 TB/s) and plateau at 25699 hashes/s because argon2_mpipe can present at most one 3-4 KiB request per cycle (3584 B/cycle average).
8 stacks vs 1 stack at 236 engines / CYC_BLOCK=260: 3229.5 vs 1227.9 B/cycle (2.63x); at the plateau 25699 vs 8864 hashes/s (2.90x). Not 8x.

CYC_BLOCK=133 (the landed write-back): with KCTX=2 the engine costs 176.5-178.6 cycles/block, not 133, because one outstanding 350-cycle request per context cannot be hidden by 2x133 cycles of compute. The knee moves 260 -> 177 engines (measured exactly 1.000 blocks/cycle at 177), not to 365, and hashes/s stay 25699 (port-bound).

The write-back therefore lowers the engine count needed and leaves the throughput ceiling where the request port puts it; turning it into throughput needs >= 3 request lanes (2.741 needed, 3 gives the 70443 hashes/s link ceiling).

Per-stack load balance is exact (12.50% each) when the port is saturated; mpipe traffic shows 12.60/12.40 (even/odd stacks) on a 60 s window because argon2_mpipe starts context c at c*(BPH/NCTX)=82c, an even block, biasing block parity.

Existing-model caveat: argon2_mpipe stores the request id in gsel[IDW-1:0]; the checked-in tb_mpipe leaves IDW=6, which is correct only up to 64 contexts (32 engines). Measured at NENG=59: 410.6 B/cycle with IDW=6 vs 811.7 B/cycle with IDW=8 (matches the 813 B/cycle in SPEED.md). This study derives IDW = clog2(NENG*KCTX).

multi_lane_request_ports.why: one request per cycle x 3584 B is 3584 B/cycle, so a single-port design uses 36% of 9.82 TB/s
multi_lane_request_ports.rtl: argon2_mpipe NPORT/NRESP (lane = engine % NPORT) + hbm3e_mem NPORT/NRESP with a response compaction network

lanes_isolated_test.how: 3 lanes always asserted, 4096 B each, 2000 cycles, block index incremented per lane
lanes_isolated_test.note: 99.7% of 9824; the 0.3% is startup, since the first requests cannot return before LAT=350

bugs_found_and_fixed_after_the_first_rep: hbm3e_mem's per-stack lane round-robin pointer was never reset, so the lane select was X, every stack rejected every request, yet req_ready read high: 0 B/cycle with 2000/2000 requests 'accepted'
hbm3e_mem's response queue gated req_ready on req_valid, which deadlocks any master that waits for ready first (the capacity testbench does exactly that forever)
the 32-deep response FIFO was replaced by a compaction network: with at most one response per stack per cycle and NRESP >= NSTACK nothing can be lost, so no queue is needed
the testbench did not pass NPORT/NRESP to hbm3e_mem, so both defaulted to 1 and the multi-lane buses were silently truncated
known_limitations: argon2_mpipe's blocks_done increments by one per cycle even when several contexts finish together, so its cycles/block and hashes/s read low above one block per cycle. The published hashes/s figures are derived from measured bytes/cycle (/3584 B per block / 38912 blocks) instead, which is why the table quotes bytes first.

the 484-engine / KCTX=2 point reached only 1592 B/cycle (0.44 blocks/cycle) instead of the ~9800 the latency model predicts; unexplained, so it is not quoted as a result. KCTX=3 with 365 engines reaches 99.8% of the link and is the configuration reported.

benchmark_8_stacks_max_cores.configuration: 8 HBM3e stacks, 3 request lanes, 3 response lanes, CYC_BLOCK=133, 1 GHz, 10,000-cycle steady window

measured.bound: memory at a realistic row-activate derate
anomalous, unexplained: KCTX=2 at the marginal engine count stalls

max_cores_the_memory_can_feed.why: 9824 B/cycle / 3584 B per block = 2.741 blocks/cycle, x 133 cycles per block per engine
max_cores_the_memory_can_feed.note: 550 engines measure 70,518 hashes/s vs 70,426 at 365: the extra 185 engines add 0.13%

capacity_is_not_the_limit.note: the memory is bought for bandwidth, not capacity; only 16% of it is needed to keep 365 engines busy

benchmark_8_stacks_max_cores.bugs_found_fixing_the_counter: blocks_done used a nonblocking +1 per completing context, so simultaneous completions collapsed into one; it now tallies a blocking temp and adds it once per edge. The earlier 25,699 result was unaffected (exactly 1 block/cycle) but every config above one block/cycle read low.

the_card_365_engines.testbench: chip/tb/tb_argon2_card.v, in TBS/sim as a fast wiring check
the_card_365_engines.command: make -C chip card-argon2-max   (NENG=365, KCTX=3, LAT=350, CYC=133)

area.note: generic yosys cells from the single-engine synth, multiplied by 365; not a synthesis run of the whole chip

what_this_proves_and_what_it_does_not: proves: BAR0 -> start pulse -> 365-engine array -> 3 lanes -> 8 stacks -> id-tagged responses all work together, at 99.5% of the memory's bandwidth, through the card's own register interface
does not prove: 365 paralleled permutations. argon2_mpipe charges each block the measured 133 cycles; 365 real argon2_fill copies is 68.1 M cells and is not simulable here
the real datapath is verified separately: tb_argon2_fill against the reference block, tb_argon2_engine against argon2-cffi, make vlreal solving a real challenge

when_the_design_is_off_the_optimum.two_contexts: 484 engines for the same 70,426 hashes/s; the latency floor is 350/2 = 175 cycles/block
